newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SOCIAL DEMS PROPOSE REWORKING OF 1997 BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SOCIAL DEMS PROPOSE REWORKING OF 1997 BUDGET.

text.p: The head of the parliamentary caucus of the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) on Wednesday submitted a bill to force changes in the government's 1997 state budget draft before a first reading in parliament.

CSSD MP Stanislav Gross, submitted a plan which, in part, would require the government to re-submit its draft budget by the end of October with limits on the transfer of funds within the budget totals, once agreed in parliament.
The CSSD proposal must go to a vote before the budget draft, which was expected to have a first reading on Wednesday, can go to the floor.

Klaus's centre-right coalition, which lost its majority in the house in June elections, has hinted it might resign if the opposition, led by the Social Democrats, succeeded in forcing changes to its planned balanced budget.

The plan submitted by CSSD would limit the government to changes during the fiscal year of a maximum five percent on the revenue side and five percent on the expenditure side of the total volume of the agreed state budget.

It would also require a rise in payments to municipalities to compensate for changes in the tax code, and would limit the mayors of major cities to determine discressionary spending of up to a maximum of 10 percent of state funds.
It is not yet clear how quickly the house will put the CSSD proposal to a vote, nor how long a vote on the first reading of the budget might be delayed.
If the measure is approved, it would delay a vote on the first reading of the state budget until at least October 30, as the government would have to recast the draft.
